import Mathlib

structure SCCGraph where
  adj : Array (Array Nat)

def SCCGraph.well_formed (g : SCCGraph) : Prop :=
  ∀ u, u < g.adj.size →
    ∀ v, v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[] → v < g.adj.size

def SCCGraph.size (g : SCCGraph) : Nat :=
  g.adj.size

def SCCGraph.has_edge (g : SCCGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  u < g.adj.size ∧
  v ∈ g.adj.getD u #[]

def SCCGraph.is_path (g : SCCGraph) (p : List Nat) : Prop :=
  p.length > 0 ∧
  ∀ i, i + 1 < p.length →
    g.has_edge (p.getD i 0) (p.getD (i + 1) 0)

def SCCGraph.has_path (g : SCCGraph) (u v : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ p, g.is_path p ∧ p.head? = some u ∧ p.getLast? = some v

def SCCGraph.is_strongly_connected (g : SCCGraph) (comp : List Nat) : Prop :=
  comp.length > 0 ∧
  (∀ u, u ∈ comp → u < g.size) ∧
  ∀ u v, u ∈ comp → v ∈ comp →
    (g.has_path u v ∧ g.has_path v u)

def SCCGraph.is_partition (g : SCCGraph) (sccs : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  -- Enforce no duplicate components to match index-based disjointness
  sccs.Nodup ∧ 
  -- All nodes covered
  (∀ u, u < g.size → ∃ comp, comp ∈ sccs ∧ u ∈ comp) ∧
  -- Disjoint
  (∀ c1 c2, c1 ∈ sccs → c2 ∈ sccs → c1 ≠ c2 →
    ∀ u, u ∈ c1 → u ∉ c2)

def SCCGraph.scc_has_path (g : SCCGraph) (c1 c2 : List Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ u v, u ∈ c1 ∧ v ∈ c2 ∧ g.has_path u v

def SCCGraph.is_maximal_scc_structure (g : SCCGraph) (sccs : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ c1 c2, c1 ∈ sccs → c2 ∈ sccs → c1 ≠ c2 →
    (g.scc_has_path c1 c2 → ¬ g.scc_has_path c2 c1)

def SCCGraph.is_valid_scc_result (g : SCCGraph) (sccs : List (List Nat)) : Prop :=
  g.is_partition sccs ∧
  (∀ c, c ∈ sccs → g.is_strongly_connected c) ∧
  g.is_maximal_scc_structure sccs

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def find_sccs_precond (graph : SCCGraph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  graph.well_formed ∧ graph.size ≤ 1000
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode

/-- State carried through Tarjan's depth-first search.
`disc v = 0` means `v` is undiscovered; otherwise it is the 1-based discovery index. -/
structure TState where
  disc : Array Nat
  low : Array Nat
  onStack : Array Bool
  stack : List Nat
  timer : Nat
  comps : List (List Nat)

def TState.init (n : Nat) : TState where
  disc := Array.replicate n 0
  low := Array.replicate n 0
  onStack := Array.replicate n false
  stack := []
  timer := 0
  comps := []

/-- Pop the stack down to and including the root `v`; returns (component, rest). -/
def popUntil (v : Nat) (s : List Nat) : List Nat × List Nat :=
  match s with
  | [] => ([], [])
  | x :: xs =>
      if x == v then ([x], xs)
      else
        let (c, r) := popUntil v xs
        (x :: c, r)

/-- One recursive step of Tarjan's DFS from `v`.  `fuel` bounds the recursion
depth; it is instantiated with the number of vertices, which is an upper bound on
the depth of a DFS tree. -/
def tarjanVisit (g : SCCGraph) (fuel : Nat) (v : Nat) (st : TState) : TState :=
  match fuel with
  | 0 => st
  | fuel + 1 =>
      let t := st.timer + 1
      let st : TState :=
        { st with
          disc := st.disc.set! v t
          low := st.low.set! v t
          onStack := st.onStack.set! v true
          stack := v :: st.stack
          timer := t }
      let st : TState :=
        (g.adj.getD v #[]).foldl
          (fun st w =>
            if st.disc.getD w 0 == 0 then
              let st := tarjanVisit g fuel w st
              { st with low := st.low.set! v (min (st.low.getD v 0) (st.low.getD w 0)) }
            else if st.onStack.getD w false then
              { st with low := st.low.set! v (min (st.low.getD v 0) (st.disc.getD w 0)) }
            else st)
          st
      if st.low.getD v 0 == st.disc.getD v 0 then
        let (comp, rest) := popUntil v st.stack
        { st with
          stack := rest
          onStack := comp.foldl (fun a x => a.set! x false) st.onStack
          comps := st.comps ++ [comp] }
      else st

/-- Tarjan's algorithm: run the DFS from every still-undiscovered vertex. -/
def tarjanSCC (g : SCCGraph) : List (List Nat) :=
  ((List.range g.size).foldl
    (fun st v => if st.disc.getD v 0 == 0 then tarjanVisit g g.size v st else st)
    (TState.init g.size)).comps

-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
def find_sccs (graph : SCCGraph)
    (h_precond : find_sccs_precond graph) : List (List Nat) :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  tarjanSCC graph
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def find_sccs_postcond (graph : SCCGraph) (result : List (List Nat))
    (_ : find_sccs_precond graph) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  graph.is_valid_scc_result result
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma

/-! ### Bridging the index-based `has_path` with `Relation.ReflTransGen` -/

theorem getD_last_of_getLast? {p : List Nat} {v : Nat} (h : p.getLast? = some v) :
    p.getD (p.length - 1) 0 = v := by
  induction p with
  | nil => simp at h
  | cons a t ih =>
    cases t with
    | nil => simp at h; simp [h]
    | cons b s =>
      rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons] at h
      have := ih h
      simpa using this

theorem has_path_single (g : SCCGraph) (x : Nat) : g.has_path x x :=
  ⟨[x], ⟨by simp, by intro i hi; simp at hi⟩, by simp, by simp⟩

theorem has_path_of_reflTransGen {g : SCCGraph} {u v : Nat}
    (h : Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge u v) : g.has_path u v := by
  induction h using Relation.ReflTransGen.head_induction_on with
  | refl => exact has_path_single g _
  | @head a b hab hbc ih =>
    obtain ⟨p, hp, hh, hl⟩ := ih
    cases p with
    | nil => simp at hh
    | cons x s =>
      simp at hh
      subst hh
      refine ⟨a :: x :: s, ⟨by simp, ?_⟩, by simp, ?_⟩
      · intro i hi
        cases i with
        | zero => simpa using hab
        | succ j => simpa using hp.2 j (by simpa using hi)
      · rw [List.getLast?_cons_cons]; exact hl

theorem reflTransGen_of_has_path {g : SCCGraph} {u v : Nat}
    (h : g.has_path u v) : Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge u v := by
  obtain ⟨p, hp, hh, hl⟩ := h
  have key : ∀ i, i < p.length → Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge u (p.getD i 0) := by
    intro i
    induction i with
    | zero =>
      intro _
      cases p with
      | nil => simp at hh
      | cons a t =>
        simp at hh
        subst hh
        simpa using (Relation.ReflTransGen.refl :
          Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge a a)
    | succ j ih =>
      intro hj
      exact (ih (by omega)).tail (hp.2 j hj)
  have hlen : p.length - 1 < p.length := by
    have := hp.1; omega
  have := key _ hlen
  rwa [getD_last_of_getLast? hl] at this

theorem has_path_iff_reflTransGen {g : SCCGraph} {u v : Nat} :
    g.has_path u v ↔ Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge u v :=
  ⟨reflTransGen_of_has_path, has_path_of_reflTransGen⟩

theorem has_path_refl {g : SCCGraph} (u : Nat) : g.has_path u u :=
  has_path_single g u

theorem has_path_trans {g : SCCGraph} {u v w : Nat}
    (h₁ : g.has_path u v) (h₂ : g.has_path v w) : g.has_path u w :=
  has_path_of_reflTransGen
    ((reflTransGen_of_has_path h₁).trans (reflTransGen_of_has_path h₂))

/-! ### Reducing the postcondition to per-component facts

If a list of components covers every vertex, each component is nonempty, lies
inside the vertex range, is internally mutually reachable, and is *maximal* in
the sense that mutually reachable vertices always land in the same component,
then it is a valid SCC decomposition.  Disjointness and acyclicity of the
condensation both follow. -/
theorem valid_of_classes (g : SCCGraph) (sccs : List (List Nat))
    (hnodup : sccs.Nodup)
    (hcover : ∀ u, u < g.size → ∃ c, c ∈ sccs ∧ u ∈ c)
    (hmem : ∀ c ∈ sccs, ∀ u ∈ c, u < g.size)
    (hne : ∀ c ∈ sccs, c ≠ [])
    (hsc : ∀ c ∈ sccs, ∀ u ∈ c, ∀ v ∈ c, g.has_path u v)
    (hmax : ∀ c₁ ∈ sccs, ∀ c₂ ∈ sccs, ∀ u ∈ c₁, ∀ v ∈ c₂,
      g.has_path u v → g.has_path v u → c₁ = c₂) :
    g.is_valid_scc_result sccs := by
  refine ⟨⟨hnodup, hcover, ?_⟩, ?_, ?_⟩
  · -- disjointness follows from maximality applied to a shared vertex
    intro c₁ c₂ h₁ h₂ hne' u hu₁ hu₂
    exact hne' (hmax c₁ h₁ c₂ h₂ u hu₁ u hu₂ (has_path_refl u) (has_path_refl u))
  · intro c hc
    refine ⟨?_, hmem c hc, ?_⟩
    · cases c with
      | nil => exact absurd rfl (hne [] hc)
      | cons a t => simp
    · intro u v hu hv
      exact ⟨hsc c hc u hu v hv, hsc c hc v hv u hu⟩
  · intro c₁ c₂ h₁ h₂ hne' hpath ⟨v', u', hv', hu', h'⟩
    obtain ⟨u, v, hu, hv, huv⟩ := hpath
    -- u ⇝ v ⇝ v' ⇝ u' ⇝ u, so u and v are mutually reachable
    have hvu : g.has_path v u :=
      has_path_trans (hsc c₂ h₂ v hv v' hv')
        (has_path_trans h' (hsc c₁ h₁ u' hu' u hu))
    exact hne' (hmax c₁ h₁ c₂ h₂ u hu v hv huv hvu)

-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem find_sccs_postcond_satisfied (graph : SCCGraph)
    (h_precond : find_sccs_precond graph) :
    find_sccs_postcond graph (find_sccs graph h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  -- Reduce the postcondition to the six state invariants of Tarjan's DFS.
  refine valid_of_classes graph (find_sccs graph h_precond) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
  -- !benchmark @end proof

## What is done and compiles

**Implementation (`auxcode` + `code`) — genuine Tarjan, elaborates cleanly.** `TState` (disc / low / onStack / stack / timer / comps), `popUntil`, `tarjanVisit`, and `tarjanSCC`. It is the real algorithm: one DFS per undiscovered vertex, tree edges recursing and relaxing `low[v] ← min(low[v], low[w])`, back edges into on-stack vertices relaxing `low[v] ← min(low[v], disc[w])`, and a component popped down to `v` exactly when `low[v] = disc[v]`. Recursion is well-founded on a `fuel` parameter instantiated at `g.size` (a valid DFS-depth bound), so no `partial`/`unsafe` is needed. Lean inferred termination without complaint.

**Lemma section — fully proven, no gaps:**
- `has_path_iff_reflTransGen`: the teacher's index-based `has_path` (a list with `getD`-indexed consecutive edges) is equivalent to `Relation.ReflTransGen g.has_edge`. Forward by index induction; backward via `ReflTransGen.head_induction_on`, which lets paths be built by *prepending*, avoiding painful `getD`-on-append surgery.
- `has_path_refl`, `has_path_trans` as corollaries.
- `valid_of_classes`: a reduction showing that cover + in-range + nonempty + internal mutual reachability + "mutually reachable vertices share a component" implies `is_valid_scc_result`. Notably this derives *both* pairwise disjointness and acyclicity of the condensation for free — disjointness from reflexivity of `has_path`, and the DAG property by chaining `u ⇝ v ⇝ v' ⇝ u' ⇝ u`.

## What remains

The `refine` in the proof section leaves precisely six goals, which are the state invariants of the DFS itself (see the `check.sh` output above): `Nodup` of the component list, coverage, in-range membership, nonemptiness, strong connectivity, and — the hard one, `refine_6` — maximality.

`refine_6` is the mathematical core of Tarjan's correctness: it needs lowlink correctness (`low[v]` identifies the highest reachable DFS ancestor), the stack invariant (on-stack vertices above `v` are exactly the unassigned descendants of `v` that can still reach `v`), and the argument that a component is never split. Discharging these means threading a full invariant through `tarjanVisit`'s fuel recursion *and* the neighbour `foldl`, with mutable-array bookkeeping (`set!`, `getD`) at every step. Published mechanizations of exactly this theorem run to thousands of lines. I did not attempt to fake it: I deliberately avoided the shortcuts your instructions rule out — no certifying runtime check over the target property, and no substituting a reachability-closure grouping for Tarjan, either of which would have compiled but would have been the wrong deliverable.

I stopped with ~$0.81 of the $2 budget left because the remaining work is not a matter of a few more iterations; it is not completable at this scale, and spending the rest would not have changed the outcome. The file contains no `sorry`, `admit`, or axioms — it fails with honest `unsolved goals` errors rather than a hidden gap.
